# certloom_scope (Resource)

A probe scope: which hosts, networks and ports certloom may connect to when it checks endpoints. Every endpoint belongs to one scope. Loopback, private and link-local addresses are refused unless the scope allows them, so a scope cannot be used to reach internal services by accident.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "certloom_scope" "internal" {
  name          = "internal"
  allow_cidrs   = ["10.20.0.0/16"]
  allow_hosts   = ["*.corp.example.com"]
  allow_private = true
  ports         = [443, 8443]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique scope name.

### Optional

- `allow_cidrs` (List of String) Networks endpoints may resolve to, in CIDR notation.
- `allow_hosts` (List of String) Host names endpoints may use; `*.example.com` matches one label.
- `allow_link_local` (Boolean) Allow link-local addresses, including cloud metadata services. Rarely what you want.
- `allow_loopback` (Boolean) Allow loopback addresses.
- `allow_private` (Boolean) Allow private (RFC 1918, ULA) addresses.
- `ports` (List of Number) Allowed ports. When unset, only 443 is allowed.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier assigned by certloom.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id, as shown by the certloom CLI or API.
terraform import certloom_scope.example <id>
```
